title: Cancer: current or history, and metastases
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's cancer as documented at this visit.
note:
Chief Complaint: Follow-up for prostate cancer.

HPI: Pt is a 66-year-old male presenting for follow-up of prostate cancer. Pt is currently receiving chemotherapy for the malignancy. He reports some fatigue and mild abdominal discomfort but denies severe pain or acute distress. He notes that the liver metastasis has been causing some dull aching over the last two weeks. He is compliant with the current treatment regimen but expresses concerns regarding the progression of the malignant neoplasm.

Medication List:
- Chemotherapy agent (current cycle)
- Ondansetron 8mg PRN for N/V
- Acetaminophen 650mg BID for pain

Review of Systems:
Constitutional: Positive for fatigue.
GI: Positive for mild abdominal discomfort.
MSK: Negative for joint pain.
Neuro: Negative for numbness or weakness.
All other systems reviewed and negative.

Social History: Retired. Lives with wife. Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol use.

Family History: Father had hypertension. Mother had diabetes.

Vitals:
BP: 132/84
HR: 78 (RRR)
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on RA
Weight: 195 lbs

Recent Labs:
WBC: 6.2
Hgb: 11.8
Plt: 145k
AST: 88
ALT: 92
Creatinine: 1.1
eGFR: 72

Exam:
Gen: Well-appearing male, in no acute distress.
CV: RRR, CTAB.
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, mild tenderness over RUQ. No rebound or guarding.
Skin: No new lesions noted.

Assessment:
1. Prostate cancer, currently receiving chemotherapy.
2. Liver metastasis, status post current treatment.

Plan:
1. Continue current chemotherapy schedule as prescribed.
2. Monitor liver function tests and abdominal symptoms.
3. Manage pain with scheduled acetaminophen; PRN ondansetron for nausea.
4. Follow up in 3 weeks for reassessment of liver metastasis and overall tolerance to treatment.

Electronically signed, E. Castillo, MD, 10/14/2026
explanations: Cancer of the prostate under current treatment is a current malignancy: C61.
Liver metastases: C78.7, secondary malignant neoplasm of liver (HCC 17).

distractors.why: Treatment is still directed at the cancer, so it is current, not history.
Metastasis is coded as a secondary malignancy, even when the primary is history.
The metastases are in the liver, not bone.

hccs.label: Cancer Metastatic to Lung/Liver/Brain/and Other Organs; Acute Myeloid Leukemia Except Promyelocytic
